sanskrit: dhūmrākṣaṃ nihataṃ śrutvā rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ balādhyakṣam uvācedaṃ kṛtāñjalim upasthitam
english: Having heard that Dhūmrākṣa was slain, Rāvaṇa, lord of the Rākṣasas, spoke these words to the commander of the army who stood before him with palms joined.

sanskrit: śīghraṃ niryāntu durdharṣā rākṣasā bhīmavikramāḥ akampanaṃ puraskṛtya sarvaśastraprakovidam
english: "Let the invincible Rākṣasas of terrible valor go forth swiftly, placing at their head Akampana, who is skilled in all weapons."

sanskrit: tato nānāpraharaṇā bhīmākṣā bhīmadarśanāḥ niṣpetū rākṣasā mukhyā balādhyakṣapracoditāḥ
english: Then the foremost Rākṣasas, bearing various weapons, with fearsome eyes and fearsome appearance, rushed forth, urged on by the commander of the army.

sanskrit: ratham āsthāya vipulaṃ taptakāñcanakuṇḍalaḥ rākasaiḥ saṃvṛto ghorais tadā niryāty akampanaḥ
english: Mounting a great chariot, his earrings of molten gold gleaming, Akampana then marched forth, surrounded by fearsome Rākṣasas.

sanskrit: na hi kampayituṃ śakyaḥ surair api mahāmṛdhe akampanas tatas teṣām āditya iva tejasā
english: Indeed Akampana could not be made to tremble even by the gods in great battle; blazing with the splendor of the sun, he shone before them.

sanskrit: tasya nidhāvamānasya saṃrabdhasya yuyutsayā akasmād dainyaṃ āgacchad dhayānāṃ rathavāhinām
english: Yet as he rushed forward, seized with eagerness for battle, a sudden distress came over the horses that drew his chariot.

sanskrit: vyasphuran nayanaṃ cāsya savyaṃ yuddhābhinandinaḥ vivarṇo mukhavarṇaś ca gadgadaś cābhavat svaraḥ
english: His left eye twitched, of him who delighted in battle; his face grew pale, and his voice became faltering.

sanskrit: abhavat sudine cāpi durdine rūkṣamārutam ūcuḥ khagā mṛgāḥ sarve vācaḥ krūrā bhayāvahāḥ
english: Though the day had been auspicious, a harsh wind arose making it inauspicious; all the birds and beasts cried out with cruel cries foreboding fear.

sanskrit: sa siṃhopacitaskandhaḥ śārdūlasamavikramaḥ tān utpātān acintyaiva nirjagāma raṇājiram
english: Yet he, with shoulders as massive as a lion's, his valor equal to a tiger's, gave no thought to those ill omens and marched out onto the battlefield.

sanskrit: tadā nirgacchatas tasya rakṣasaḥ saha rākṣasaiḥ babhūva sumahān nādaḥ kṣobhayann iva sāgaram
english: As that Rākṣasa marched out together with his Rākṣasas, a tremendous roar arose, as if shaking the ocean itself.

sanskrit: tena śabdena vitrastā vānarāṇāṃ mahācamūḥ drumaśailapraharaṇā yoddhuṃ samavatiṣṭhata
english: Alarmed by that sound, the great army of monkeys, armed with trees and rocks, stood ready for battle.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ yuddhaṃ mahāraudraṃ saṃjajñe kapirakṣasām rāmarāvaṇayor arthe samabhityaktajīvinām
english: Between those monkeys and Rākṣasas a terrible battle arose, for the sake of Rāma and Rāvaṇa, among those who had utterly cast away their lives.

sanskrit: sarve hy atibalāḥ śūrāḥ sarve parvatasaṃnibhāḥ harayo rākṣasāś caiva parasparajighaṃsavaḥ
english: All were exceedingly strong, all were heroic, all — monkeys and Rākṣasas alike — resembled mountains, and all were eager to slay one another.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ vinardātāṃ śabdaḥ saṃyuge 'titarasvinām śuśruve sumahān krodhād anyonyam abhigarjatām
english: The tremendous sound of those swift combatants roaring in battle could be heard as they bellowed furiously at one another.

sanskrit: rajaś cāruṇavarṇābhaṃ subhīmam abhavad bhṛśam uddhūtaṃ harirakṣobhiḥ saṃrurodha diśo daśa
english: Dust of a deep reddish hue, exceedingly dreadful and thick, stirred up by the monkeys and Rākṣasas, blocked all ten directions.

sanskrit: anyonyaṃ rajasā tena kauśeyoddhūtapāṇḍunā saṃvṛtāni ca bhūtāni dadṛśur na raṇājire
english: In that dust, white as silk shaken out, the beings on the battlefield could not see one another at all, so thoroughly were they covered.

sanskrit: na dhvajo na patākāvā varma vā turago 'pi vā āyudhaṃ syandanaṃ vāpi dadṛśe tena reṇunā
english: Neither banner, nor flag, nor armor, nor horse, nor weapon, nor chariot — none could be seen in that dust.

sanskrit: śabdaś ca sumahāṃs teṣāṃ nardatām abhidhāvatām śrūyate tumule yuddhe na rūpāṇi cakāśire
english: In that tumultuous battle only the tremendous sound of those roaring warriors charging could be heard; their forms were not visible.

sanskrit: harīn eva susaṃkruddhā harayo jaghnur āhave rākṣasāś cāpi rakṣāṃsi nijaghnus timire tadā
english: In that darkness, furious monkeys struck down monkeys in battle, and Rākṣasas likewise slew Rākṣasas.

sanskrit: parāṃś caiva vinighnantaḥ svāṃś ca vānararākṣasāḥ rudhirārdraṃ tadā cakrur mahīṃ paṅkānulepanām
english: Slaying enemies and allies alike, the monkeys and Rākṣasas at that time made the earth sodden with blood, smeared as if with mud.

sanskrit: tatas tu rudhiraugheṇa siktaṃ vyapagataṃ rajaḥ śarīraśavasaṃkīrṇā babhūva ca vasuṃdharā
english: Then, drenched by the flood of blood, the dust settled; and the earth became strewn with corpses and body parts.

sanskrit: drumaśaktiśilāprāsair gadāparighatomaraiḥ harayo rākṣasās tūrṇaṃ jaghnur anyonyam ojasā
english: With trees, spears, rocks, javelins, clubs, iron bars, and pikes, the monkeys and Rākṣasas quickly struck each other with might.

sanskrit: bāhubhiḥ parighākārair yudhyantaḥ parvatopamāḥ harayo bhīmakarmāṇo rākṣasāñ jaghnur āhave
english: Fighting with arms shaped like iron bars, those monkeys like mountains, performers of terrible deeds, struck down the Rākṣasas in battle.

sanskrit: rākṣasāś cāpi saṃkruddhāḥ prāsatomarapāṇayaḥ kapīn nijaghnire tatra śastraiḥ paramadāruṇaiḥ
english: The furious Rākṣasas too, javelins and pikes in hand, slew the monkeys there with exceedingly dreadful weapons.

sanskrit: harayas tv api rakṣāṃsi mahādrumamahāśmabhiḥ vidārayanty abhikramya śastrāṇy ācchidya vīryataḥ
english: But the monkeys, advancing against the Rākṣasas with great trees and great boulders, tore them apart and shattered their weapons by force.

sanskrit: etasminn antare vīrā harayaḥ kumudo nalaḥ maindaś ca paramakruddhaś cakrur vegam anuttamam
english: Meanwhile, the heroic monkeys Kumuda, Nala, and Mainda, exceedingly enraged, exerted their utmost speed.

sanskrit: te tu vṛkṣair mahāvegā rākṣasānāṃ camūmukhe kadanaṃ sumaha cakrur līlayā hariyūthapāḥ
english: Those monkey chiefs, with great speed, wrought tremendous slaughter at the forefront of the Rākṣasa army with trees, as if in sport.

sanskrit: tad dṛṣṭvā sumahat karma kṛtaṃ vānarasattamaiḥ krodham āhārayām āsa yudhi tīvram akampanaḥ
english: Witnessing that great feat accomplished by those foremost of monkeys, Akampana summoned fierce anger in battle.

sanskrit: krodhamūrchitarūpas tu dhnuvan paramakārmukam dṛṣṭvā tu karma śatrūṇāṃ sārathiṃ vākyam abravīt
english: His form overcome with rage, twanging his supreme bow, and having witnessed the deeds of the enemies, he spoke these words to his charioteer:

sanskrit: tatraiva tāvat tvaritaṃ rathaṃ prāpaya sārathe ete 'tra bahavo ghnanti subahūn rākṣasān raṇe
english: "Drive the chariot quickly to that very spot, charioteer — these many foes are slaying very many Rākṣasas in battle."

sanskrit: ete 'tra balavanto hi bhīmakāyāś ca vānarāḥ drumaśailapraharaṇās tiṣṭhanti pramukhe mama
english: "These monkeys here are powerful and of fearsome frame; armed with trees and rocks they stand before me."

sanskrit: etān nihantum icchāmi samaraślāghino hy aham etaiḥ pramathitaṃ sarvaṃ dṛśyate rākṣasaṃ balam
english: "I, who glory in battle, wish to slay them — for the entire Rākṣasa force is seen to have been shattered by them."

sanskrit: tataḥ prajavitāśvena rathena rathināṃ varaḥ harīn abhyahanat krodhāc charajālair akampanaḥ
english: Then Akampana, best of chariot warriors, borne in his chariot by swift horses, struck the monkeys in anger with nets of arrows.

sanskrit: na sthātuṃ vānarāḥ śekuḥ kiṃ punar yoddhum āhave akampanaśarair bhagnāḥ sarva eva pradudruvuḥ
english: The monkeys were unable to stand their ground, much less fight in battle; shattered by Akampana's arrows, they all fled in panic.

sanskrit: tān mṛtyuvaśam āpannān akampanavaśaṃ gatān samīkṣya hanumāñ jñātīn upatasthe mahābalaḥ
english: Seeing those kinsmen fallen under the sway of death, come under Akampana's power, the mighty Hanūmān stood forth to protect them.

sanskrit: taṃ mahāplavagaṃ dṛṣṭvā sarve plavagayūthapāḥ sametya samare vīrāḥ sahitāḥ paryavārayan
english: Seeing that great monkey, all the heroic monkey chiefs assembled in battle and surrounded Hanūmān together.

sanskrit: vyavasthitaṃ hanūmantaṃ te dṛṣṭvā hariyūthapāḥ babhūvur balavanto hi balavantam upāśritāḥ
english: Those monkey leaders, seeing Hanūmān stationed there, became strong themselves — for the strong take refuge with the strong.

sanskrit: akampanas tu śailābhaṃ hanūmantam avasthitam mahendra iva dhārābhiḥ śarair abhivavarṣa ha
english: But Akampana poured arrows down upon Hanūmān standing there like a mountain, just as Mahendra pours rain with streams of water.

sanskrit: acintayitvā bāṇaughāñ śarīre patitāñ śitān akampanavadhārthāya mano dadhre mahābalaḥ
english: Giving no thought to the sharp arrows that had fallen upon his body in floods, the mighty one fixed his mind on killing Akampana.

sanskrit: sa prahasya mahātejā hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ abhidudrāva tad rakṣaḥ kampayann iva medinīm
english: Then, laughing aloud, the mighty Hanūmān, son of the Wind, charged at that Rākṣasa, shaking the very earth as he ran.

sanskrit: tasyābhinardamānasya dīpyamānasya tejasā babhūva rūpaṃ durdharṣaṃ dīptasyeva vibhāvasoḥ
english: Of him who charged with a roar, blazing with splendor, there appeared a form irresistible, like that of blazing fire.

sanskrit: ātmānaṃ tv apraharaṇaṃ jñātvā krodhasamanvitaḥ śailam utpāṭayām āsa vegena haripuṃgavaḥ
english: Knowing himself to be without a weapon at hand, that bull among monkeys, filled with rage, uprooted a mountain with speed.

sanskrit: taṃ gṛhītvā mahāśailaṃ pāṇinaikena mārutiḥ vinadya sumahānādaṃ bhrāmayām āsa vīryavān
english: Taking that great mountain in one hand, the mighty son of the Wind, letting out a tremendous roar, began to whirl it.

sanskrit: tatas tam abhidudrāva rākṣasendram akampanam yathā hi namuciṃ saṃkhye vajreṇeva puraṃdaraḥ
english: Then he charged at Akampana, lord of Rākṣasas, just as Purandara charged at Namuci in battle with his thunderbolt.

sanskrit: akampanas tu tad dṛṣṭvā giriśṛṅgaṃ samudyatam dūrād eva mahābāṇair ardhacandrair vyadārayat
english: But Akampana, seeing that mountain peak raised aloft, split it from a distance with great crescent-headed arrows.

sanskrit: tat parvatāgram ākāśe rakṣobāṇavidāritam vikīrṇaṃ patitaṃ dṛṣṭvā hanūmān krodhamūrchitaḥ
english: Seeing that mountain peak split by the Rākṣasa's arrows and falling scattered through the sky, Hanūmān was overcome with rage.

sanskrit: so 'śvakarṇaṃ samāsādya roṣadarpānvito hariḥ tūrṇam utpāṭayām āsa mahāgirim ivocchritam
english: That monkey, filled with fury and pride, quickly went to an Aśvakarṇa tree and uprooted it as if it were a great risen mountain.

sanskrit: taṃ gṛhītvā mahāskandhaṃ so 'śvakarṇaṃ mahādyutiḥ prahasya parayā prītyā bhrāmayām āsa saṃyuge
english: Taking that Aśvakarṇa tree of great trunk, that one of great splendor, laughing with extreme delight, whirled it in battle.

sanskrit: pradhāvann uruvegena prabhañjaṃs tarasā drumān hanūmān paramakruddhaś caraṇair dārayat kṣitim
english: Running with great speed, swiftly shattering trees, Hanūmān, supremely enraged, split the earth with his feet.

sanskrit: gajāṃś ca sagajārohān sarathān rathinas tathā jaghāna hanumān dhīmān rākṣasāṃś ca padātikān
english: The wise Hanūmān slew elephants with their riders, charioteers with their chariots, and Rākṣasa foot soldiers as well.

sanskrit: tam antakam iva kruddhaṃ samare prāṇahāriṇam hanūmantam abhiprekṣya rākṣasā vipradudruvuḥ
english: Seeing Hanūmān in battle, angry as Death itself, a taker of life, the Rākṣasas fled in all directions.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ saṃkruddhaṃ rākṣasānāṃ bhayāvaham dadarśākampano vīraś cukrodha ca nanāda ca
english: The heroic Akampana saw him charging, supremely wrathful, the terror of Rākṣasas; he grew furious and bellowed.

sanskrit: sa caturdaśabhir bāṇaiḥ śitair dehavidāraṇaiḥ nirbibheda hanūmantaṃ mahāvīryam akampanaḥ
english: Akampana pierced the mighty Hanūmān with fourteen sharp arrows that rent the body.

sanskrit: sa tathā pratividdhas tu bahvībhiḥ śaravṛṣṭibhiḥ hanūmān dadṛśe vīraḥ prarūḍha iva sānumān
english: Though thus pierced by those many showers of arrows, the heroic Hanūmān appeared like a mountain in full bloom.

sanskrit: tato 'nyaṃ vṛkṣam utpāṭya kṛtvā vegam anuttamam śirasy abhijaghānāśu rākṣasendram akampanam
english: Then, uprooting another tree, and exerting his utmost speed, he quickly struck Akampana, lord of Rākṣasas, on the head.

sanskrit: sa vṛkṣeṇa hatas tena sakrodhena mahātmanā rākṣaso vānarendreṇa papāta sa mamāra ca
english: Struck by that tree by the great-souled lord of monkeys in his wrath, that Rākṣasa fell and died.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā nihataṃ bhūmau rākṣasendram akampanam vyathitā rākṣasāḥ sarve kṣitikampa iva drumāḥ
english: Seeing Akampana, lord of Rākṣasas, struck down upon the earth, all the Rākṣasas were shaken like trees in an earthquake.

sanskrit: tyaktapraharaṇāḥ sarve rākṣasās te parājitāḥ laṅkām abhiyayus trastā vānarais tair abhidrutāḥ
english: All those defeated Rākṣasas, having abandoned their weapons, fled terrified to Laṅkā, chased by those monkeys.

sanskrit: te muktakeśāḥ saṃbhrāntā bhagnamānāḥ parājitāḥ sravacchramajalair aṅgaiḥ śvasanto vipradudruvuḥ
english: They fled in panic, hair loose, pride shattered, defeated, panting, their bodies streaming with sweat.

sanskrit: anyonyaṃ pramamantus te viviśur nagaraṃ bhayāt pṛṣṭhatas te susaṃmūḍhāḥ prekṣamāṇā muhur muhuḥ
english: They stumbled against one another and entered the city out of fear, completely bewildered, glancing back again and again.

sanskrit: teṣu laṅkāṃ praviṣṭeṣu rākṣaseṣu mahābalāḥ sametya harayaḥ sarve hanūmantam apūjayan
english: When those Rākṣasas had entered Laṅkā, all the mighty monkeys assembled and honored Hanūmān.

sanskrit: so 'pi prahṛṣṭas tān sarvān harīn saṃpratyapūjayat hanūmān sattvasaṃpanno yathārham anukūlataḥ
english: And Hanūmān, endowed with excellence, joyful in return, honored all those monkeys fittingly and graciously.

sanskrit: vineduś ca yathā prāṇaṃ harayo jitakāśinaḥ cakarṣuś ca punas tatra saprāṇān eva rākṣasān
english: The monkeys roared with the breath of victory and dragged back there the Rākṣasas who were still alive.

sanskrit: sa vīraśobhām abhajan mahākapiḥ sametya rakṣāṃsi nihatya mārutiḥ mahāsuraṃ bhīmam amitranāśanaṃ yathaiva viṣṇur balinaṃ camūmukhe
english: That great monkey, the son of the Wind, having slain the Rākṣasas and that terrible great Asura, destroyer of enemies, bore the glory of a hero — just as Viṣṇu at the forefront of battle slew the mighty Bali.

sanskrit: apūjayan devagaṇās tadā kapiṃ svayaṃ ca rāmo 'tibalaś ca lakṣmaṇaḥ tathaiva sugrīvamukhāḥ plavaṃgamā vibhīṣaṇaś caiva mahābalas tadā
english: The hosts of gods honored that monkey at that time; and mighty Rāma himself, and Lakṣmaṇa of exceeding strength, and likewise the monkeys headed by Sugrīva, and the mighty Vibhīṣaṇa — all honored him then.

sanskrit: akampanavadhaṃ śrutvā kruddho vai rākṣaseśvaraḥ kiṃ cid dīnamukhaś cāpi sacivāṃs tān udaikṣata
english: Having heard of the slaying of Akampana, the lord of Rākṣasas grew furious; his face somewhat downcast, he looked upon his ministers.

sanskrit: sa tu dhyātvā muhūrtaṃ tu mantribhiḥ saṃvicārya ca purīṃ pariyayau laṅkāṃ sarvān gulmān avekṣitum
english: After reflecting for a moment and deliberating with his ministers, he went around the city of Laṅkā to inspect all the garrisons.

sanskrit: tāṃ rākṣasagaṇair guptāṃ gulmair bahubhir āvṛtām dadarśa nagarīṃ laṅkāṃ patākādhvajamālinīm
english: He saw the city of Laṅkā, protected by hosts of Rākṣasas, surrounded by many garrisons, garlanded with banners and flags.

sanskrit: ruddhāṃ tu nagarīṃ dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ uvācāmarṣitaḥ kāle prahastaṃ yuddhakovidam
english: Seeing the city besieged, Rāvaṇa, lord of Rākṣasas, in his anger spoke at the right moment to Prahasta, skilled in warfare:

sanskrit: purasyopaniviṣṭasya sahasā pīḍitasya ca nānyaṃ yuddhāt prapaśyāmi mokṣaṃ yuddhaviśārada
english: "For a city suddenly besieged and oppressed, I see no other deliverance than battle, O master of warfare.

sanskrit: ahaṃ vā kumbhakarṇo vā tvaṃ vā senāpatir mama indrajid vā nikumbho vā vaheyur bhāram īdṛśam
english: "I, or Kumbhakarṇa, or you my general, or Indrajit, or Nikumbha — one of us must bear such a burden.

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ balam itaḥ śīghram ādāya parigṛhya ca vijayāyābhiniryāhi yatra sarve vanaukasaḥ
english: "Therefore, taking and marshaling the army swiftly from here, go forth for victory to where all those forest dwellers are."

sanskrit: niryāṇād eva te nūnaṃ capalā harivāhinī nardatāṃ rākṣasendrāṇāṃ śrutvā nādaṃ draviṣyati
english: "Surely upon your mere march out, the fickle monkey host will flee upon hearing the roar of the Rākṣasa lords."

sanskrit: capalā hy avinītāś ca calacittāś ca vānarāḥ na sahiṣyanti te nādaṃ siṃhanādam iva dvipāḥ
english: "For monkeys are fickle, undisciplined, and unstable of mind; they will not endure your roar, just as elephants cannot endure a lion's roar."

sanskrit: vidrute ca bale tasmin rāmaḥ saumitriṇā saha avaśaste nirālambaḥ prahastavaśam eṣyati
english: "And when that army is scattered in flight, Rāma together with the son of Sumitrā will remain helpless without support, and will come under Prahasta's power."

sanskrit: āpatsaṃśayitā śreyo nātra niḥsaṃśayīkṛtā pratilomānulomaṃ vā yad vā no manyase hitam
english: "In calamity, the better course is the one fraught with doubt, not the certain one — or weigh what you consider favorable, for or against."

sanskrit: rāvaṇenaivam uktas tu prahasto vāhinīpatiḥ rākṣasendram uvācedam asurendram ivośanā
english: Thus addressed by Rāvaṇa, Prahasta, commander of the army, spoke these words to the lord of Rākṣasas, as Uśanā speaks to the lord of Asuras:

sanskrit: rājan mantritapūrvaṃ naḥ kuśalaiḥ saha mantribhiḥ vivādaś cāpi no vṛttaḥ samavekṣya parasparam
english: "O king, we took counsel before with skilled ministers, and debate too arose among us as we examined the matter from every side.

sanskrit: pradānena tu sītāyāḥ śreyo vyavasitaṃ mayā apradāne punar yuddhaṃ dṛṣṭam etat tathaiva naḥ
english: "By the return of Sītā I determined that the better course lay; but in the case of not returning her, battle was likewise seen by us to be the outcome.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ dānaiś ca mānaiś ca satataṃ pūjitas tvayā sāntvaiś ca vividhaiḥ kāle kiṃ na kuryāṃ priyaṃ tava
english: "I, who have been constantly honored by you with gifts, honor, and various conciliations — how at this moment should I not do what is dear to you?

sanskrit: na hi me jīvitaṃ rakṣyaṃ putradāradhanāni vā tvaṃ paśya māṃ juhūṣantaṃ tvadarthe jīvitaṃ yudhi
english: "My life is not to be guarded, nor my sons, wife, or wealth — behold me offering up my life in battle for your sake."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu bhartāraṃ rāvaṇaṃ vāhinīpatiḥ samānayata me śīghraṃ rākṣasānāṃ mahad balam
english: Having thus spoken to his lord Rāvaṇa, the army commander said: "Bring me quickly the great force of Rākṣasas."

sanskrit: madbāṇāśanivegena hatānāṃ tu raṇājire adya tṛpyantu māṃsena pakṣiṇaḥ kānanaukasām
english: "Today let the birds feast on the flesh of those forest dwellers slain in battle by the thunderbolt speed of my arrows."

sanskrit: ity uktās te prahastena balādhyakṣāḥ kṛtatvarāḥ balam udyojayām āsus tasmin rākṣasamandire
english: Thus addressed by Prahasta, the army commanders, making haste, mobilized the army in that Rākṣasa palace.

sanskrit: sā babhūva muhūrtena tigmanānāvidhāyudhaiḥ laṅkā rākṣasavīrais tair gajair iva samākulā
english: Within a moment Laṅkā was crowded with those heroic Rākṣasas bearing sharp and various weapons, thronging like elephants.

sanskrit: hutāśanaṃ tarpayatāṃ brāhmaṇāṃś ca namasyatām ājyagandhaprativahaḥ surabhir māruto vavau
english: As they propitiated the sacred fire and paid homage to the Brāhmaṇas, a fragrant wind blew carrying the scent of clarified butter.

sanskrit: srajaś ca vividhākārā jagṛhus tv abhimantritāḥ saṃgrāmasajjāḥ saṃhṛṣṭā dhārayan rākṣasās tadā
english: The Rākṣasas, ready for battle and joyful, took garlands of various kinds consecrated with sacred formulas and wore them then.

sanskrit: sadhanuṣkāḥ kavacino vegād āplutya rākṣasāḥ rāvaṇaṃ prekṣya rājānaṃ prahastaṃ paryavārayan
english: The Rākṣasas, bearing bows and clad in armor, leaped up with speed, and gazing upon King Rāvaṇa, surrounded Prahasta.

sanskrit: athāmantrya ca rājānaṃ bherīm āhatya bhairavām āruroha rathaṃ divyaṃ prahastaḥ sajjakalpitam
english: Then, having taken leave of the king and beating the dreadful war drum, Prahasta mounted his divine chariot, fully equipped and made ready.

sanskrit: hayair mahājavair yuktaṃ samyak sūtasusaṃyutam mahājaladanirghoṣaṃ sākṣāc candrārkabhāsvaram
english: Yoked with horses of great speed, properly fitted with a skilled charioteer, its sound like a great cloud's thunder, blazing like the sun and moon themselves —

sanskrit: uragadhvajadurdharṣaṃ suvarūthaṃ svapaskaram suvarṇajālasaṃyuktaṃ prahasantam iva śriyā
english: — Irresistible with its serpent-banner, well-fitted with a hood, bearing good arms, covered with a net of gold, and as if laughing with splendor —

sanskrit: tatas taṃ ratham āsthāya rāvaṇārpitaśāsanaḥ laṅkāyā niryayau tūrṇaṃ balena mahatā vṛtaḥ
english: Then Prahasta, executing the command entrusted by Rāvaṇa, mounted that chariot and quickly marched out of Laṅkā, surrounded by a great army.

sanskrit: tato duṃdubhinirghoṣaḥ parjanyaninadopamaḥ śuśruve śaṅkhaśabdaś ca prayāte vāhinīpatau
english: Then as the army commander marched forth, the sound of kettledrums like the rumble of rain clouds was heard, and the sound of conches as well.

sanskrit: ninadantaḥ svarān ghorān rākṣasā jagmur agrataḥ bhīmarūpā mahākāyāḥ prahastasya puraḥsarāḥ
english: Rākṣasas of fearsome form and massive frame, roaring with terrible cries, marched at the fore as Prahasta's vanguard.

sanskrit: vyūḍhenaiva sughoreṇa pūrvadvārāt sa niryayau gajayūthanikāśena balena mahatā vṛtaḥ
english: He marched out by the eastern gate in battle-array, exceedingly terrible, surrounded by a great army resembling a herd of elephants.

sanskrit: sāgarapratimaughena vṛtas tena balena saḥ prahasto niryayau tūrṇaṃ kruddhaḥ kālāntakopamaḥ
english: Surrounded by that army resembling the ocean's flood, Prahasta marched out swiftly, wrathful, his anger like that of Death at the end of an age.

sanskrit: tasya niryāṇa ghoṣeṇa rākṣasānāṃ ca nardatām laṅkāyāṃ sarvabhūtāni vinedur vikṛtaiḥ svaraiḥ
english: At the sound of his march and the roaring of the Rākṣasas, all creatures in Laṅkā cried out with distorted voices.

sanskrit: vyabhram ākāśam āviśya māṃsaśoṇitabhojanāḥ maṇḍalāny apasavyāni khagāś cakrū rathaṃ prati
english: Birds that feed on flesh and blood, entering the cloudless sky, circled in inauspicious spirals toward his chariot.

sanskrit: vamantyaḥ pāvakajvālāḥ śivā ghorā vavāśire
english: Jackals, dreadful and terrible, howled, vomiting flames of fire.

sanskrit: antarikṣāt papātolkā vāyuś ca paruṣo vavau anyonyam abhisaṃrabdhā grahāś ca na cakāśire
english: A meteor fell from the sky, a harsh wind blew, and the planets, in conflict with one another, shone not at all.

sanskrit: vavarṣū rudhiraṃ cāsya siṣicuś ca puraḥsarān ketumūrdhani gṛdhro 'sya vilīno dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ
english: Rain of blood fell upon him and drenched his vanguard; a vulture perched atop his standard facing south.

sanskrit: sārather bahuśaś cāsya saṃgrāmam avagāhataḥ pratodo nyapatad dhastāt sūtasya hayasādinaḥ
english: As his charioteer plunged repeatedly into battle, the goad fell from the hand of the chariot-driver who guided the horses.

sanskrit: niryāṇa śrīś ca yāsyāsīd bhāsvarā ca sudurlabhā sā nanāśa muhūrtena same ca skhalitā hayāḥ
english: The radiant glory of victory that had attended his march — dazzling and exceedingly rare — vanished in a moment, and on level ground his horses stumbled.

sanskrit: prahastaṃ tv abhiniryāntaṃ prakhyāta balapauruṣam yudhi nānāpraharaṇā kapisenābhyavartata
english: But against Prahasta who marched forth, renowned for his strength and valor, the monkey army bearing various weapons advanced for battle.

sanskrit: atha ghoṣaḥ sutumulo harīṇāṃ samajāyata vṛkṣān ārujatāṃ caiva gurvīś cāgṛhṇatāṃ śilāḥ
english: Then a tremendous din arose from the monkeys as they tore up trees and seized heavy boulders.

sanskrit: ubhe pramudite sainye rakṣogaṇavanaukasām vegitānāṃ samarthānām anyonyavadhakāṅkṣiṇām parasparaṃ cāhvayatāṃ ninādaḥ śrūyate mahān
english: Both armies were eager — the hosts of Rākṣasas and the forest dwellers — swift, capable, each hungering to slay the other; a great din was heard as they challenged one another.

sanskrit: tataḥ prahastaḥ kapirājavāhinīm abhipratasthe vijayāya durmatiḥ vivṛddhavegāṃ ca viveśa tāṃ camūṃ yathā mumūrṣuḥ śalabho vibhāvasum
english: Then Prahasta, of evil mind, charged at the monkey king's army for victory, and entered that swelling force with its growing momentum — as a moth seeking death enters fire.
